title: How does one surgeon do 2,000 operations?
principle: One standard way of working cuts cost and mistakes.

screens.text: Let me tell you about an eye hospital in Madurai. Aravind Eye Hospital does cataract operations, which clear cloudy eyes. An Aravind surgeon does about 2,000 a year; the Indian average is 250. Yet its patients have about half the problems after surgery that Britain's do. Have a guess how.

screens.prompt: How do you think Aravind's surgeons can do so many operations, and safely?

options.label: Its doctors work far longer hours
Each job is done one fixed way
It buys costly machines from abroad

screens.why: Each job is done one fixed way, every time. While a surgeon operates on one patient, the next one is already being made ready. The surgeon does only the key steps, and trained helpers do the rest in the same order, like a factory line. When every step is fixed, a mistake stands out.

screens.title: Standard work
screens.text: This is called standard work: one written best way for each job, which everyone follows. Toyota's car factories made it famous. It isn't about working harder. When everyone works the same way, a mistake shows up fast, and one fix helps everyone. Does everyone in your shop pack the same way?

screens.title: Now look at your bakery
screens.text: Now picture your home bakery in August of its fifth year. Your sister and your cousin now bake with you, about 30 cakes a week, at ₹850 each. But their chocolate cakes don't taste like yours, because each of you has your own way.

screens.prompt: You bake 30 cakes a week. 3 go wrong, and baking each one again costs you ₹400. What do the mistakes cost a month?
screens.why: Exactly. 3 cakes × ₹400 is ₹1,200 a week, and 4 weeks make ₹4,800 a month. You keep ₹450 on a ₹850 cake, so that's more than ten cakes' worth of profit, lost to three different ways of baking.

wrong.a: That's one week: 3 × ₹400 = ₹1,200. A month has about 4 weeks, so the mistakes cost ₹4,800.
wrong.c: I see what you did: 3 × ₹850 × 4. But you don't lose the price. You lose what it costs to bake again: 3 × ₹400 × 4 weeks = ₹4,800.

screens.prompt: You'll write your chocolate cake on one card. I'll show you six notes. For each one, tell me: should it go on the card?

items.text: Cocoa: 60 grams, weighed on the scale
Add sugar until it tastes right
Bake it the way Mummy did
Done when a knife comes out clean

screens.why: Exactly. A standard card says things anyone can check: grams, a temperature, a time, a test. "Until it tastes right", "the way Mummy did" and "beat it well" mean something different to each person. Write "beat for 4 minutes" instead.

screens.prompt: Here are five steps for bringing in standard work, mixed up. Put them in the right order.
steps: Bake your best cake, and weigh everything
Write the weights, times and checks on one card
Show your helpers, then watch each one bake once
Check every cake against the card
When someone finds a better way, test it and update the card
screens.why: Exactly. First find your best way and measure it, then write it down, teach it, and check it. The last step matters most: a standard isn't fixed forever. When anyone finds a better way, it becomes the new card for everyone.

screens.prompt: Your cousin skipped the card and guessed the sugar. Her cake came out perfect. Was her way a good way?

options.label: Yes. It worked, so her way works
Only if the customer liked it
No. She may not get it right next time

screens.why: Right. Remember Unit 1: judge the thinking, not the luck. A guess can work once. The card works every time, for anyone, and that's what lets three people bake one cake.

wrong.a: The cake was perfect this time. But remember Unit 1: judge the thinking, not the luck. Guessing the sugar can go wrong next time, and nobody would know why.
wrong.b: The customer's happiness matters, but it can't tell you if guessing will work next time. Judge the thinking, not the luck. The card works every time.

screens.prompt: Your sister finds that whisking 5 minutes longer makes the cake lighter. Customers notice. What should you do?

options.label: Try it on a few cakes, then decide
Tell her to follow the card as written
Let her whisk longer on her own cakes

screens.why: Exactly. Standard work doesn't mean nobody may improve. It means the best way so far, written down. Try her idea on a few cakes. If it works, it goes on the card, so every cake gets lighter, not just hers.

wrong.b: The card is the best way so far, not forever. Try her idea on a few cakes. If it really works, put it on the card, so every cake gets lighter.
wrong.c: Then her cakes and yours taste different again. Test her idea, and if it works, change the card for everyone.

screens.setup: It's late August. A café wants 10 chocolate cakes every Friday, all exactly alike. It buys many, so it pays ₹700 each. Each costs ₹400 to make, so you'd keep ₹3,000 a week. Your sister and cousin will bake most of them.
screens.question: How do you get ready for the café?

options.label: Bake them yourself. It's only 10 cakes
options.outcome: The café's cakes are all alike, and you keep ₹3,000 a week. But you bake till midnight every Thursday, and in two weeks your home orders start to slip.
options.why: You got the cakes right, but only you can make them. That way, the business can't grow past your own hands.
options.better: Write a card, bake the first batch with your helpers, and check it.

options.label: Bake the first batch together, with a card
options.outcome: You write the card and bake the first batch together. One cake fails your check, so that week you keep ₹2,600, and you fix that step on the card. After that, all 10 match every week. You keep ₹3,000 a week, and your Thursday nights are free.
options.why: Exactly. The card let three people bake one cake. Checking the first batch found the weak step early, and the fix reached everyone at once.

options.label: Give them the card, and taste every cake
options.outcome: The card helps, but nobody watched them bake. Your cousin reads "60 g" as a heaped spoon. Each Friday one cake tastes wrong, and you bake it again: you keep ₹2,600 a week. The café is happy, but you spend Friday mornings fixing cakes.
options.why: The card was the right start. But a card nobody has tried out together leaves room for each person to read it their own way.
options.better: Write the card, bake the first batch together, and check it.

screens.text: Three tailors cut shirts three ways, so the sleeves never ___. One written ___ way would fix it.
screens.why: Exactly. Same job, three ways, three results. Write the one best way down, teach it, and the shirts match, just like your cakes.

summary: Standard work: one written best way for each job, which everyone follows.
Write things anyone can check: grams, temperatures, times and tests.
When someone finds a better way, test it and change the card for everyone.

cards.front: Three helpers bake the same cake three ways, and some cakes fail. What fixes it?
options: Taste every cake at the end
cards.back: Standard work: one written best way that everyone follows.

cards.front: Which line belongs on a standard recipe card?
cards.back: Write things anyone can check: grams, temperatures, times.

cards.front: A helper finds a better way to do one step. What now?
options: Test it, then change the card for all
Tell her to follow the card
cards.back: A standard is the best way so far. Improve it for everyone.
